newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish money markets calm after Erbakan remarks.
newsitem.headline: Turkish money markets calm after Erbakan remarks.

text.p: Turkish financial markets kept calm at mid-day as Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said he was ready for new elections at any moment.
Bankers said there was no sharp reaction to Erbakan's words in the market, already cautious over political developments in recent days.
Turkish bond rates remained steady at 97.5-98 percent levels, unchanged from Tuesday's opening as central bank funding through overnight repos keep interest rates relatively low.
The lira traded firmer at 135,290 per dollar, from 135,350 morning, but was weaker from 135,200 Monday close.
Overnight money rates are running at around the opening level of 71.75 percent.

"Today at any moment, whoever wants it, we are ready for elections," Erbakan told his Islam-based Welfare Party (RP) amid intensified opposition efforts to bring down his coalition with the conservative True Path Party.

Bulent Ecevit, leader of the Democratic Left Party, is holding talks with other opposition leaders on forming a government excluding the RP, at odds with the army over the implementation of anti-Islamist measures.
Erbakan also said the opposition could not mount a credible alternative to his coalition government.
